families.name: Monophosphines
families.note: Trialkyl- and triarylphosphines, by size and donor strength.

families.name: Dialkylbiaryl phosphines
families.note: Buchwald-type ligands for cross-coupling, drawn with the PR₂ group kept as a label.

families.name: Other bulky monophosphines
families.note: Ligands for difficult couplings that are not biaryls.

families.name: Bis- and polyphosphines
families.note: Chelating phosphines, by bite angle; PR₂ groups kept as labels.

families.name: Chiral bisphosphines
families.note: For asymmetric hydrogenation and other enantioselective reactions; one enantiomer is drawn (mirror it for the other).

families.name: P,N ligands
families.note: Phosphinooxazolines and other ligands with one P and one N donor.

families.name: Phosphoramidites
families.note: Monodentate BINOL- and spirobiindane-based ligands (Feringa, Zhou).

families.name: N-Heterocyclic and other carbenes
families.note: Bonded through the carbene carbon; S- in front means the saturated (imidazolin-2-ylidene) ring.

families.name: Bipyridines, phenanthrolines and terpyridines
families.note: Chelating diimines, the workhorses of Ni, Cu and photoredox catalysis.

families.name: Diamines, polyamines and aza-macrocycles
families.note: Chelating sp³ N-donors, chiral diamines for transfer hydrogenation, and tripodal and macrocyclic amines.

families.name: Bis(oxazolines) and pyridine-oxazolines
families.note: C₂-symmetric BOX and PyBOX ligands for Cu, Zn, Fe and Ni; one enantiomer is drawn.

families.name: Imines, salens and cyclometallating ligands
families.note: Diimines, β-diketiminates, salens, porphyrins and C^N ligands for Ir and Pt emitters.

families.name: Pincers
families.note: Tridentate ligands that hold the metal in a plane: PNP, PCP, POCOP, NCN, PNN and MACHO.

families.name: O-donors: diketonates, carboxylates, diolates
families.note: Anionic O-ligands (X-type) and the chiral diols used as ligands.

families.name: Solvents, oxides and crown ethers
families.note: Neutral O-donors (L-type): coordinating solvents, phosphine oxides and the crowns and cryptands that hold alkali metals.

families.name: π-Ligands and carbonyl
families.note: Cyclopentadienyls, arenes, dienes and allyls, drawn in perspective on the metal.

ligands.name: 3,3′,3′′-Phosphanetriyltris(benzenesulfonic acid)
ligands.note: Water-soluble; sold as the trisodium salt.

ligands.name: 2-(Diphenylphosphino)pyridine
ligands.note: Usually bonds through P alone, or bridges two metals through P and N.

ligands.name: Bis(diphenylphosphino)methane
ligands.note: Bridges two metals more often than it chelates one.

ligands.name: (1R,2R)-N-(p-Toluenesulfonyl)-1,2-diphenylethylenediamine
ligands.note: Noyori's transfer-hydrogenation ligand: NH₂ gives a lone pair, NTs is an amide (X).

ligands.name: 2,6-Bis[1-(2,6-diisopropylphenylimino)ethyl]pyridine (Dipp-PDI)
ligands.note: Redox non-innocent pincer for Fe and Co (Brookhart, Gibson, Chirik).

ligands.name: 2-Phenylpyridine (C^N)
ligands.note: Cyclometallated at the phenyl ring's ortho carbon, as in Ir(ppy)₃.

ligands.name: α,α,α′,α′-Tetramethyl-1,3-benzenedipropanoate (esp)
ligands.note: Bridges two Rh atoms in Rh₂(esp)₂.

ligands.name: Dimethyl sulfoxide (O-bound)
ligands.note: Hard metals take DMSO through O; Ru, Pd and Pt often through S.
